messages:
maria: quick heads-up — noticed a weird UX edge with the Insights widget: sticky filters persist when you switch from a per-route view to the global model view and then back; the route-specific telemetry shown afterwards is wrong :confused:

gabe: ahh, reproable? steps?

maria: open route A insights -> apply filters (status:production, model:p68) -> click 'All Models' quick toggle -> click back to route A. The filter pill still shows model:p68 but the telemetry is aggregated across models in the UI.

taylor: hmm that sounds like state desync between the route-scoped filter store and the widget's model scope. Could be our route-to-model binding codepath. Any console errors?

maria: no console errors, but saw this in the trace logs:
```
INFO: widget: applyFilters route=A scope=route model= p68
DEBUG: route-store: switched to all-models
INFO: widget: render scope=all-models filter=MODEL:p68
```
so UI kept the pill but the backend query changed.

priya: is this limited to sticky filters or affects saved queries too?

maria: saved queries seem okay — they serialize explicit scope. Sticky/ephemeral filters are only in client state.

gabe: two problems here: 1) mismatch confuses users (wrong telemetry), 2) sampling/telemetry attribution might record metrics under wrong route/model if we send events on UI change without scope reconciliation. We should avoid emitting telemetry events until scope sync confirmed.

taylor: agree. Proposed fix: on scope toggle, widget should first reconcile filter scope -> if mismatch, clear model-specific pills or transform them to global equivalents, then fetch. Also add guard in telemetry client to tag events with asserted scope id.

priya: +1. For rollout UX, we can ship a non-breaking client patch that clears ephemeral model pills on route toggle and add a feature-flag to rehydrate them only when explicit. Then follow with a more polished retain/transform behavior.

maria: timeline? this affects a small percent of users but can produce misleading cost/latency numbers on dashboards (we saw one ops ticket).

gabe: I'll file a quick bug with repro steps and add unit tests for scope reconciliation. Can we also add an integration test that checks telemetry tags after scope transitions?

maria: please — add an e2e that simulates: apply filters -> toggle -> toggle back -> assert fetch query contains scope=route and telemetry event includes route_id.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch/gabe/fix-sticky-filter -> staging (ETA 12m) :rocket:

taylor: follow-ups: (1) UX copy: show a subtle badge when filters are discarded due to scope mismatch, (2) console: surface that telemetry events are delayed until fetch completes.

priya: can product owner approve the badge text? i propose: "Filter adjusted to match view - view-specific filters were cleared" — too wordy?

maria: "Filters reset to match current view" shorter.

gabe: logging notes: ensure any automatic discard/transform emits an audit event so we can debug in support tickets.

maria: ok good plan. I'll add the UX mock and link the ticket to the rollout plan. Thanks all.
